name: Glide
tagline: No-code app builder for portals, dashboards, and mobile-style apps

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Maker around $49/month annual-effective and roughly $60/month monthly.

tiers.name: GlideOS Free
tiers.limits: 1 project; 1 app; 100 MB storage; 2 team members; credit allowance described only as limited
tiers.notes: This is the current GlideOS product, separate from legacy Glide Classic subscriptions.

tiers.name: GlideOS Solo
tiers.limits: 5 projects; unlimited apps; 25 GB storage; 2 team members; starts at 100 credits
tiers.notes: Additional credit pricing is not publicly fixed on the page.

tiers.name: GlideOS Team
tiers.limits: 20 projects; unlimited apps; 100 GB storage; 5 members; starts at 500 credits + 50 per extra member

tiers.name: GlideOS Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom projects, members, storage, credits, support and security

pricing.freeTierCaps: GlideOS: 1 project, 1 app, 100 MB storage and 2 team members; the official page calls the credit allowance 'limited' without a numeric cap
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only on the current GlideOS page; no annual price shown
pricing.hiddenCosts: GlideOS credits are a separate consumption meter and higher usage may require add-ons; the current GlideOS subscription is not the same product as Glide Classic, which can require a separate legacy subscription

verdictSummary: You can build one specific Glide app; you are not rebuilding the no-code app builder, data editor, permissions, and deployment platform in one sitting.
coreLoopDIY: Build the specific portal/dashboard needed using a normal web framework and database rather than rebuilding Glide itself.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because building one app is easier than becoming the developer for every future app change.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Open-source no-code database; combine with a frontend for many Glide-like apps.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: A table workspace plus an app builder for portals and mobile-style screens; visual polish is lower, data ownership is better.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Its app builder lacks Glide's mobile-first polish, touch-friendly components, action system, and near-native app feel.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Internal apps, forms, automations, and portals in one box; much closer to Knack than its developer branding suggests.

facts.install: Docker image or Docker Compose; Kubernetes is also supported
facts.engines: Model-agnostic; the agent builder supports bring-your-own AI provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Built-in app data and app definitions are stored in CouchDB, files in MinIO/S3-compatible object storage, and connected external data remains in its source system
facts.gapVsPaid: Budibase is a responsive web internal-tool builder, not a mobile-first app platform, so Glide's polished phone experience is the main sacrifice.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker and persistent storage; production use also means owning upgrades, TLS, backups, and database/network access

alternatives.name: Glide Free
alternatives.desc: The same builder works indefinitely for one simple Glide-table app and ten personal users; integrations wait behind payment.

facts.dataFormat: The free plan uses Glide Tables or Big Tables stored in Glide's infrastructure; Glide Tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same product under tight limits, with integrations, scale, branding control, and more capable production workflows reserved for paid plans.

alternatives.name: NocoBase
alternatives.desc: A database-backed app builder with pages, forms, roles, workflows, and enough plugins to become your next maintenance hobby.

facts.install: NocoBase CLI or Docker deployment with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Built-in AI employees can connect to common LLMs; exact provider support depends on installed AI plugins
facts.dataFormat: Business data lives in standard relational tables in the configured MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; files use configured local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: NocoBase builds browser-based database apps but does not provide Glide's refined mobile navigation, components, and installable-app experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a database, secrets, and deployment administration; the community license also preserves NocoBase branding and restricts some uses

alternatives.name: Softr Free
alternatives.desc: A friendlier portal and dashboard builder with real users, forms, record actions, workflows, and a free published app.

facts.dataFormat: App definitions and any Softr Database records live in Softr's cloud; connected-source records remain in the external source, with Softr proxying requests and caching data for up to 24 hours; table blocks can export CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: Softr is stronger at portals and websites than mobile-style operational apps, so Glide's touch interactions and phone-first workflow are noticeably weaker.
facts.setupBlocker: No software install; the first hurdle is choosing and authenticating a data source, then mapping its fields and permissions

notes: Important distinction: vibecode the app, not the app builder.
prompt:
Build me the one mobile-friendly data app I would have made in Glide. Requirements:

- Do not rebuild the no-code builder, build the single app: a CRUD portal over
  one dataset. Example to implement: a client directory with jobs and
  statuses; swap in my real columns at the top of the schema file.
- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered with htmx for inline edits,
  no build step, no frontend framework.
- Import: a script that loads the Google Sheets CSV export the Glide app
  currently runs on into SQLite.
- List view with search and column filters, a detail view, add/edit forms, all
  laid out to work one-handed on a phone screen.
- Access for a small trusted crew: one shared secret token in the URL path,
  read from .env, served over HTTPS on my VPS. No user accounts.
- /export returns the current data as CSV so I am never locked in.
- No telemetry; the data lives in one SQLite file I can back up by copying.
- Out of scope: a drag-and-drop builder, per-user permissions, native mobile
  apps. When the app needs to change, I change the code.
- README: import steps, deploy notes, and how to rotate the access token.
